question_text: An 18-month-old boy is brought in to the pediatrician by his mother for concerns that her child is becoming more and more yellow over the past two days. She additionally states that the boy has been getting over a stomach flu and has not been able to keep down any food. The boy does not have a history of neonatal jaundice. On exam, the patient appears slightly sluggish and jaundiced with icteric sclera. His temperature is 99.0°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 88/56 mmHg, pulse is 110/min, and respirations are 22/min. His labs demonstrate an unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia of 16 mg/dL. It is determined that the best course of treatment for this patient is phenobarbital to increase liver enzyme synthesis. Which of the following best describes the molecular defect in this patient?

                    ### Question
                    An 18-month-old boy is brought in to the pediatrician by his mother for concerns that her child is becoming more and more yellow over the past two days. She additionally states that the boy has been getting over a stomach flu and has not been able to keep down any food. The boy does not have a history of neonatal jaundice. On exam, the patient appears slightly sluggish and jaundiced with icteric sclera. His temperature is 99.0°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 88/56 mmHg, pulse is 110/min, and respirations are 22/min. His labs demonstrate an unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia of 16 mg/dL. It is determined that the best course of treatment for this patient is phenobarbital to increase liver enzyme synthesis. Which of the following best describes the molecular defect in this patient?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Deletion in the SLCO1B1 gene
opb. Silent mutation in the UGT1A1 gene
opc. Mutation in the promoter region of the UGT1A1 gene
opd. Missense mutation in the UGT1A1 gene
ope. Nonsense mutation in the UGT1A1 gene

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The molecular defect in this patient is a missense mutation in the UGT1A1 gene, leading to reduced enzyme activity and impaired bilirubin conjugation. This defect results in unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia, jaundice, and icteric sclera. The treatment with phenobarbital aims to induce the UGT1A1 gene, increasing bilirubin conjugation and improving bilirubin metabolism.
